(af_latin_writing_system_class): Updated.

* src/autofit/aftypes.h (AF_StyleMetricsRec): Add `reverse_charmap` field.

findings.title: Signed integer overflow in af_move_contour_vertically due to plain '+=' on FT_Pos
findings.message: In af_move_contour_vertically(), each point's y coordinate is adjusted with a plain `point->y += movement;`. `point->y` is an `FT_Pos` (a signed integer type, typically `FT_Long`/`FT_Int32` depending on configuration) and `movement` is an `FT_Int`. This function is part of the new 'vertical separation adjustment' feature and is called with movement values derived from glyph bounding-box computations that can, for maliciously crafted or degenerate fonts (extreme point coordinates and overlapping contours), be far enough from zero that `point->y + movement` exceeds the representable range of the signed type, causing signed integer overflow. Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in C and was flagged by OSS-Fuzz (UBSan) in issue 499135336. The fix replaces the raw addition with the `ADD_LONG` macro, which performs the addition using unsigned arithmetic (wrap-around, well-defined) before reinterpreting/clamping back to the signed result, avoiding UB while preserving the intended saturizing/wrapping behavior used elsewhere in FreeType for pointer/coordinate arithmetic.
findings.suggestion: Use the existing `ADD_LONG` overflow-safe addition macro (already used throughout FreeType for signed pointer/coordinate math) instead of a raw `+=` when adding `movement` to `point->y`, so the operation cannot trigger undefined signed-overflow behavior on adversarial or degenerate glyph outlines.
findings.suggestion_code:
point->y = ADD_LONG( point->y, movement );
point    = point->next;

ground_truth.root_cause: The new af_move_contour_vertically() function, introduced along with the vertical separation adjustment feature, performs raw signed addition (`point->y += movement;`) without using FreeType's overflow-safe arithmetic helper macros (e.g. `ADD_LONG`), which are used elsewhere in the codebase precisely to avoid undefined behavior from signed integer overflow when combining glyph coordinate values with computed adjustments.
